info.title: Arker Public VM API
info.description: Public VM API contract. Backends expose the same endpoint and wire shapes; backend-specific feature limitations are returned as standard ErrorResponse bodies with code "unsupported_operation".

parameters.name: region
parameters.description:
Narrow to a single backend region (e.g. `us-west-2`). When omitted,
the response aggregates across every configured region.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description:
Narrow to a single backend provider. `aws` returns only
arkerd-managed (host-backed) VMs; `aws-burst` returns only
Lambda-managed VMs. When omitted, both are returned merged.

200.description: VMs visible to the authenticated caller.

post.description: Fork a VM. Optional network, disk, and resource overrides may return ErrorResponse code "unsupported_operation" on backends that do not support those options.
Run a command. Foreground command execution is required; optional background, session, resource, network, signal, and release behavior may return ErrorResponse code "unsupported_operation".

get.description: Get background run status. Backends without background runs return ErrorResponse code "unsupported_operation".

delete.description: Cancel a background run. Backends without background runs return ErrorResponse code "unsupported_operation".

get.description: List persistent sessions. Backends without persistent sessions return ErrorResponse code "unsupported_operation".

post.description: Create a persistent session. Backends without persistent sessions return ErrorResponse code "unsupported_operation".

delete.description: Delete a persistent session. Backends without persistent sessions return ErrorResponse code "unsupported_operation".

post.description: Resize VM resources. Backends without VM resize support return ErrorResponse code "unsupported_operation".

Multi-op endpoint over the VM's filesystem.

- `read` reads a file from the VM filesystem.
- `write` writes one or more files (inline chunks or presigned uploads).
- `create` ensures a `Filesystem` exists (creating one if necessary, when
  `create_if_missing: true`) and bind-mounts it into the VM at `mount_path`.
  Bidirectional by virtue of being a mount — there is no separate
  sync-direction parameter.

get.description:
List persistent filesystems owned by the authenticated caller's
organization. Filesystems are created implicitly via
`POST /v1/vms/{id}/sync` with `op: "create"` and persist independently
of any single VM.

delete.description:
Delete a persistent filesystem. The filesystem must not be mounted by
any VM at the time of deletion. Backends without filesystem persistence
return ErrorResponse code "unsupported_operation".

UnsupportedOperation.description: The request is valid, but this backend does not support the requested operation or option. The response body uses ErrorResponse with code "unsupported_operation".

value.message: background runs are not supported on this backend

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code. "unsupported_operation" means the backend does not implement the requested optional feature.

ErrorResponse.description: Standard API error. Backends use code "unsupported_operation" when the request is valid but names an operation or option this backend cannot support.

VmState.description:
Unified lifecycle state for a VM or a Session. `idle` means the
VM/session exists but no command is currently executing; `running`
means a command is in flight.

RunState.description:
Unified lifecycle state for a Run. `cancelled` covers both client
cancellation and server-side abort. Failure is NOT a state — failed
runs land in `completed` with a non-zero `exit_code`.

started_at.description: Wall-clock timestamp the session was most recently started.

region.description:
Backend region the VM lives in (e.g. `us-west-2`). With `provider`
this fully addresses the VM's routing target:
`https://{provider}-{region}.arker.ai/...`.

provider.description:
Backend provider — `aws` for arkerd-managed host-backed VMs,
`aws-burst` for Lambda-managed VMs. Together with `region`
this is enough to construct the per-VM backend URL.

started_at.description: Wall-clock timestamp the VM was most recently started (cold-boot or restored from snapshot).

host_id.description: Identifier of the worker host that owns this VM. Set by workers so a router can populate its DbCache without a PlanetScale lookup. Optional for backwards compatibility — single-host deployments and pre-split clients may omit / ignore it.

session_id.description: Optional persistent session id. Backends without persistent sessions return unsupported_operation when this is requested.

session_idx.description: Optional session selector by integer index instead of ULID. Mutually exclusive with session_id.

background.description: Run asynchronously. Backends without background execution return unsupported_operation and must not silently run the command synchronously.

vcpu_count.description: Optional per-run resource override. Backends without resource override support return unsupported_operation when this is requested.

network.description: Optional network/tunnel request. Backends without networking support return unsupported_operation when this is requested.

release.description: Optional release selection. Backends without release selection support return unsupported_operation when this is requested.

signal.description: Optional session signal. Backends without signal support return unsupported_operation when this is requested.

RunRequest.description: Foreground command execution is the portable baseline. Optional session, background, resource, network, signal, and release fields may return ErrorResponse code "unsupported_operation" on backends that do not support them.

RunResponse.description: Successful run result. BackgroundRunResponse is returned only by backends that support background runs; unsupported modes return ErrorResponse code "unsupported_operation".

dispatch.description: Which dispatch backend ran this command ("brush" or "fc"). Optional.

RunSummary.description:
Listing record for `GET /v1/vms/{id}/runs`. Every field is also
present on `Run` with the same name and type — `RunSummary` is a
strict field-subset of `Run`.

CreateSessionRequest.description: Create a persistent session. Backends without persistent sessions return unsupported_operation.

ResizeRequest.description: Resize VM resources. Backends without VM resize support return unsupported_operation.

Filesystem.description:
Org-scoped persistent filesystem. Created implicitly via
`POST /v1/vms/{id}/sync { op: "create", ... }` and managed via
`GET /v1/filesystems` and `DELETE /v1/filesystems/{filesystem_id}`.

filesystem_id.description: Address an existing filesystem by ID. Mutually exclusive with filesystem_name + create_if_missing.

filesystem_name.description: Address a filesystem by user-assigned name within the calling org. Combined with create_if_missing=true will create the filesystem if no filesystem with that name exists.

mount_path.description: VM-side path to mount the filesystem under.

SyncCreateRequest.description:
Ensure a filesystem exists (creating one if requested) and bind-mount
it into this VM at `mount_path`. Bidirectional by virtue of being a
mount.
